intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that developmental and epileptic encephalopathy-123 (DEE123) is caused by homozygous mutation in the HECW2 gene.

checks.claim: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy-123 (DEE123) is caused by homozygous mutation in the HECW2 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Thus this study describes the first homozygous HECW2 variant, inherited as an autosomal recessive pattern, contrasting with former reported de novo variants found in HECW2 patients.
checks.explanation: The paper reports a homozygous HECW2 variant in a single proband with a neurodevelopmental disorder that includes seizures, and calls this an 'association'. It does not use the DEE123 designation or establish causation on its own.

paragraphs.text: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy-123 (DEE123) is an autosomal recessive severe neurodevelopmental disorder. Features reported in affected individuals include global developmental delay, intellectual disability, hypotonia, and seizures, which may be drug-resistant. Some patients have had microcephaly, failure to thrive, and brain MRI abnormalities, including cerebral and cerebellar atrophy (Krami et al., 2022; Rodriguez-Garcia et al., 2022; Dehghanzad et al., 2025).

paragraphs.text: In a proband from a consanguineous Moroccan family with DEE123, Krami et al. (2022) identified a homozygous nonsense mutation in the HECW2 gene (c.736C-T; R246X). The mutation was found by whole-exome sequencing. The authors noted that this contrasted with the de novo heterozygous HECW2 variants previously reported in patients with neurodevelopmental disorders.

paragraphs.text: In a Caucasian girl with DEE123, Rodriguez-Garcia et al. (2022) identified a homozygous deletion-insertion in the HECW2 gene (g.197092814_197092824delinsC) by whole-exome sequencing. The mutation disrupted the splice donor site of intron 22 and caused skipping of exon 22 (r.3766_3917+1del), resulting in an in-frame deletion (p.Leu1256_Trp1306del). Functional studies showed a twofold increase in RNA expression, but protein expression was reduced by 60%. The authors suggested a partial loss-of-function mechanism.

paragraphs.text: In a 6-year-old girl of consanguineous Afghan descent with DEE123, Dehghanzad et al. (2025) identified a homozygous 1-bp insertion in the HECW2 gene (c.3601_3602insT), predicted to cause a frameshift and premature termination (Tyr1201LeufsTer7). The mutation was found by whole-exome sequencing and confirmed by Sanger sequencing. Both clinically unaffected parents were heterozygous carriers. The authors predicted that the variant would result in nonsense-mediated mRNA decay. They suggested a loss-of-function mechanism that differs from the mechanism of the missense variants associated with autosomal dominant disease.

agent.process_note: I read all three papers in full, but only their abstracts were available. Each reports a single patient with a homozygous HECW2 variant. No HGNC reference data was supplied, so the intro leaves out the gene's MIM number and chromosome location rather than filling them in from memory. None of the abstracts gives the patient's age, sex or ancestry, or segregation data, beyond what is written here. The splice variant is given only at the genomic, RNA and protein levels, with no c. notation. That variant's name (11-BP DEL/1-BP INS) is worked out from its genomic coordinates and may not match the name OMIM would give it.
